identity_resolution.frozen_upstream: The frozen Models.dev lab entry was copied from its OpenRouter mistralai/mistral-large provider record. The last lab-file commit predates the freeze, and its pinned contents match the frozen factual values.
identity_resolution.note: This is an undated alias with mixed-era metadata. OpenRouter's exact model and endpoints responses explicitly describe Mistral Large 2 (2407), while preserving a February 26, 2024 created timestamp. That timestamp agrees with the original Mistral Large/2402 launch and is retained as alias history, not the release date of Large 2. Architecture, counts and open-weight/license assessments below apply to the provider-described 2407 revision. No inference call or backend-weight attestation was performed.
conflicts: OpenRouter reports knowledge_cutoff 2024-11-30 despite describing revision 2407; this inconsistency prevents treating all provider metadata as exact checkpoint evidence.

Mistral documents the dated 2407 endpoint as retired March 30, 2025, whereas OpenRouter currently lists Mistral provider endpoints for its undated alias. The endpoints response does not expose the dated backend API name.
The February 2024 original is explicitly 32k text-only in first-party documentation, so the frozen 128k cannot be attributed to that original release.

Mistral's mistral-large-latest alias is now documented on Large 3, which is distinct from OpenRouter's undated mistralai/mistral-large alias. Do not transfer Large 3/4 MoE counts or multimodal capabilities.

It matches the frozen February date, closed-weight assertion, 128000 context and PDF input. This establishes provenance, not the model specifications.

sources.title: Frozen-era Models.dev OpenRouter alias mapping
sources.evidence: The exact OpenRouter provider file maps base_model to mistral/mistral-large, establishing that this audit record derives from OpenRouter's undated alias rather than an explicitly dated 2402 checkpoint.

sources.title: OpenRouter exact Mistral Large alias and provider metadata
sources.evidence: The exact alias is named Mistral Large; description explicitly identifies Mistral Large 2, revision mistral-large-2407. created=1708905600 is 2024-02-26 UTC. Lists Mistral provider endpoints with 128000 context and tools/tool_choice. This is primary evidence of OpenRouter's documented mapping, not proof of actual backend weights. The separate /api/v1/models response agrees but has an inconsistent November 2024 knowledge cutoff.

sources.title: Au Large: original Mistral Large announcement
sources.evidence: Dated February 26, 2024; explicitly releases Mistral Large/2402 with text generation, multilingual/code capabilities, 32K context and native function calling. Supports the original name/date history, not the later 123B or 128k specifications.

sources.title: Mistral Large 1.0 exact version documentation
sources.evidence: Explicitly maps Large 1.0 to mistral-large-2402; release February 26, 2024, text input/output, 32k context and retirement June 16, 2025. It provides no parameter-count or architecture disclosure.

sources.title: Mistral Large 2.0 exact version and weights table
sources.evidence: Identifies mistral-large-2407 and July 24, 2024 release. Its exact linked weights row separately lists Parameters (B)=123 and Active (B)=123, MRL license and 128k context. This is a nominal first-party count for 2407, not a count inferred from the model family or dense architecture. Dated endpoint is marked retired March 30, 2025.

sources.title: Mistral Large 2.0 structured documentation
sources.evidence: Explicitly lists revision 24.07, release July 24, 2024, text input, text output, 128k context, open weights linked to Mistral-Large-Instruct-2407, 123B parameters and MRL. Distinguishes native modalities from provider PDF processing.

sources.title: Mistral Large Instruct 2407 official model card
sources.evidence: Exact pinned card explicitly calls this a dense 123B language model, describes multilingual/coding capabilities, native function calling/JSON, 128k context and Mistral Research License. Gives weight-download and Transformer inference examples. README is accessible; direct config/params requests returned HTTP 401 from the license-gated repository, so no exact tensor recount is claimed.

sources.title: Large Enough: Mistral Large 2 release
sources.evidence: July 24, 2024 announcement explicitly distinguishes Large 2 from previous Mistral Large; specifies 123 billion parameters, 128k context, research-license weights and native parallel/sequential function calling. Names API revision mistral-large-2407 and links the instruct weights.

sources.title: Official 2407 repository metadata and chat template
sources.evidence: Returns repository revision a286006d554cb37a61d13c7ae61bc90cc1d372fc, gated=auto, MRL metadata, MistralForCausalLM/model_type=mistral, and the exact text/tool chat template. It does not provide a dedicated thinking-mode declaration. Gating is not evidence that weights were never released.

sources.title: OpenRouter PDF input processing
sources.evidence: Indexed primary page says PDFs work for any model; when native file input is absent OpenRouter parses the file before forwarding results. For models without image support only parsed text is forwarded. Supports removing PDF from native model modalities while recording the provider feature. The web reader accessed the complete page; direct urllib requests returned HTTP 403.

sources.title: Mistral Large 2.1 comparison for identity separation
sources.evidence: Explicitly identifies a separate 2411 revision released November 18, 2024 with its own linked weights. Its November date/capabilities are not substituted for the OpenRouter description's 2407 mapping.

sources.title: Mistral Large 3 alias and architecture comparison
sources.evidence: Maps Mistral's own mistral-large-latest alias to Large 3/2512 and specifies a 675B-total/41B-active multimodal MoE. This is a different alias/model; none of these specifications are assigned to this OpenRouter-derived entry.

sources.title: Magistral reasoning-model announcement
sources.evidence: June 10, 2025 announcement describes Magistral as Mistral's first reasoning model. This contextual distinction was checked, but is not used as an exact negative declaration of a reasoning mode for the undated Mistral Large alias.

name.note: Official original name and current OpenRouter alias name agree. Preserve the alias name; its underlying revision requires the explicit caveat above.

developer.note: Mistral AI is the model developer; preserve the catalog's normalized Mistral label. OpenRouter is the alias provider, not the developer.

family.note: Original announcement and exact Large 2 card establish the Mistral Large lineage. Family does not establish checkpoint identity.

release_date.note: Retain the first public alias/name date, corroborated by OpenRouter created timestamp and the explicit original launch. It is not the release date of the currently provider-described 2407 revision, which is July 24, 2024. Day precision is justified.

open_weights.note: The alias is documented as 2407, whose official announcement, card and docs explicitly release instruct weights under MRL. Correct false for the provider-described revision. This does not claim that original 2402 weights were released or that the alias's actual served weights were independently identified.

license.note: Published weight license for the provider-described 2407 model is MRL; the announcement distinguishes noncommercial research permission from separately acquired commercial self-deployment licensing. API service terms are a separate layer.

parameters_b.note: Nominal 123 billion parameters explicitly published for the provider-described 2407 revision. No exact full-checkpoint tensor count was performed; protected config/params requests returned HTTP 401. This count must not be attributed to the February 2402 model.

active_parameters_b.note: The official exact-2407 weights table separately reports Active (B)=123. Preserve its nominal precision; this is not inferred by equating dense total and active counts and is not an exact per-token parameter recount.

architecture.note: Exact 2407 official card explicitly says dense; repository metadata names MistralForCausalLM and the card uses the official Transformer implementation. This pertains to the provider-described revision and does not transfer the later Large 3/4 MoE architecture.

context_window.note: Keep the provider-documented 128000-token limit, independently consistent with exact 2407 first-party 128k documentation. The original 2402 had 32k, so the retained date must be understood as alias history.

modalities.note: The provider-described 2407 model is explicitly text-to-text. Clear PDF from native modalities: OpenRouter's PDF feature parses files and forwards extracted content to nonnative models; it is not evidence of a native PDF/vision encoder.

reasoning.note: The exact card describes mathematical/reasoning performance, not a dedicated thinking mode. The provider parameter list and exact template expose no reasoning control, but omission and the later Magistral announcement do not establish an explicit negative for this undated alias. Clear unsupported false; do not reinterpret general reasoning ability as reasoning-mode support.

tool_call.note: Exact 2407 official card and release explicitly establish native function calling, including parallel/sequential calls, corroborated by the exact template and OpenRouter alias's tools/tool_choice support.

description.value: Mistral Large alias, documented by OpenRouter as the dense 123B Mistral Large 2 (2407) text model with function calling.
description.note: Replace timeless flagship wording with the documented alias identity and supported capabilities. This avoids presenting 2407 facts as specifications of the February 2024 original or claiming a verified live backend.

patch.notes: Undated OpenRouter-derived alias: February 26, 2024 is its original-name/listing history. OpenRouter currently describes revision 2407, released July 24, 2024; dense architecture and nominal 123B total/123B active, open weights and MRL refer to that documented revision, not original 2402. Actual backend weights were not verified; OpenRouter's later knowledge cutoff and Mistral's retired 2407 endpoint conflict with a literal live-revision reading. Native input is text; PDF is provider parsing. Dedicated reasoning-mode support remains unverified.

summary: Resolved the frozen entry as an OpenRouter-derived undated alias with mixed-era metadata. Preserve February 26, 2024 alias/name history while explicitly identifying the provider-described Large 2 (2407) revision released July 24. For that documented revision, add nominal 123B total and separately published 123B active, dense architecture, open weights and MRL; retain 128000 context and function calling, remove native PDF and clear unsupported reasoning=false. Do not claim backend verification: the provider's November knowledge cutoff and Mistral's dated-endpoint retirement remain unresolved. Original 2402 and later Large 2.1/3/4 specifications were kept separate.
